text:
Anika: Heads-up 1 opened a PR to streamline the Dedicated provisioning doc: clarify SLA table, add micro-examples for autoscale and isolation tags. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4491
Tom: On it. Main gap: customers ask what to expect when reserved nodes are reclaimed. We should call out emergency reclamation vs planned maintenance.
Rafael: I'll paste a compact terraform snippet and a 6-line k8s-style policy. Tom: please ensure wording uses 'preemption (eviction)' once then 'preemption' afterwards.
Rafael: Terraform: ```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "blue" {
  name = "blue-prod"
  min_capacity = 3
  max_capacity = 15
  isolation = "tenant"
}
```
Rafael: K8s-like policy: ```yaml
scalePolicy:
  mode: target_utilization
  target: 0.7
  minReplicas: 3
  maxReplicas: 15
```
Priya: Add one-line note: 'isolation="tenant" reserves nodes for a single customer; preemption only in emergency reclaim.' Also add sentence: 'Latency SLOs cover committed capacity; burst is best-effort.'
Jonah: DocsBot flagged docs/dedicated#reserved-pools anchor earlier. I'll add explicit anchor and crosslink to the runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-eviction
DocsBot: link-checker: reported broken anchor -> fixed after Jonah's push.
Anika: Can we include a 2-line canary policy example under rollouts? e.g., route 5% to new model, rollback if error_rate>0.8% or p95>600ms.
Tom: Also add a tiny routing-policy blurb comparing 'latency-first' vs 'cost-first' routing choices. One sentence.
Rafael: Pushing snippets now.
DocsBot: CI: docs-build passed, link-checker passed.
Anika: Great. I'll merge after a short docs review pass. Thanks all.
